messages:
alex: kicked off a quick experiment this morning — 'token-hedging' queueing on canary pool (hedge-canary-3). Targets: keep route-level p95 <= 220ms. Canary routes: /chat-default (tier:free), /chat-pro (tier:paid).

alex: brief on the heuristic: dynamic token budgets per request + small hedging margin. Starting params: free_budget=10, paid_budget=30, hedging_factor=1.15, enable_prefix-kv-prefetch=true. Running for 30m to gather p95 + KV hit stats.

infra-bot: canary deployed to pool 'hedge-canary-3' (commit abc123). Traffic split: 1% of production sessions. :rocket:

maria: initial 15m snapshot: baseline (prod) vs canary
- /chat-default (free): baseline p95=320ms -> canary p95=240ms
- /chat-pro (paid): baseline p95=180ms -> canary p95=175ms
- KV hit-rate overall dropped ~8% on long-context (>=2048 tokens) requests on canary.

maria: notable: token-efficiency improved for short-turn (<64 tokens) completions, batching better, but long-context sufferers likely due to batching reordering + prefetch timing.

sam: microprofile dump (sample):
```
route=/chat-default samples=100
avg_queue_wait=12.4ms
avg_kernel_select=1.8ms
kernel_switch_rate=0.035/s
p95_inference=210ms
kv_hit_rate=0.62
```

sam: baseline kernel_switch_rate was ~0.02/s and avg_kernel_select=1.2ms. So canary increased kernel decision cost ~+0.6ms and more switches — seems correlated with aggressive prefetch + hedging.

lee: question — is the kernel selection policy toggling between int8-quant and fp16 paths per-batch because hedging changes effective sequence length distribution? If so, that could explain the switch spike.

maria: yes — we observed more batches with mixed sequence length profiles; runtime picks different kernels mid-batch when the max_seq estimate changes after hedging. That forces a recompile/patch path in a few cases.

toni: saw a perf regression on /embed-bulk (not in canary) last night — prob cross-pool interference? Could aggressive hedging in canary affect shared kernel caches on nodes?

sam: log snippet from a node in the canary pool: 
```
[2026-03-18T09:14:22Z] kernel_cache_evictions=12
[2026-03-18T09:14:22Z] kernel_load_latency_ms=4.1
[2026-03-18T09:14:22Z] batch_mismatch_count=7
```

sam: kernel_cache_evictions ticked up during the canary window. Evictions are cheap individually but if they coincide with many hedged batches you get transient tail noise.

lee: OK — two hypotheses: (1) hedging nudges seq-length estimates causing more kernel flavor churn; (2) queue policy allowing cross-route micro-batches to interleave increases mixed-batch composition. Either raises kernel switch rate.

alex: proposed mitigations:
- enforce route-aware micro-batch isolation when seq-length variance > threshold
- hold kernel selection stable per-worker for N seconds after load (kernel stickiness)
- reduce hedging_factor to 1.05 for free tier, keep paid at 1.15
- adapt prefetch window: delay KV prefetch for suspected long-context until batch locks

alex: quick config I pushed to the canary:
```json
{
  "route_isolation": {
    "enabled": true,
    "seq_variance_threshold": 0.35
n  },
  "kernel_stickiness_ms": 2500,
  "hedge_factors": {"free": 1.05, "paid": 1.15},
  "prefetch_delay_ms": 10
}
```

maria: re-run after the change (5m snapshot): /chat-default p95 dropped to 225ms, /chat-pro stable at 172ms, kv-hit recovered ~+4% on long-context. Kernel_switch_rate down to 0.024/s. :eyes:

toni: nice. Any impact on throughput or cost? Hedging reduction for free will reduce token-eligible batching; might increase per-token overhead.

sam: throughput delta negligible at 1% traffic. Cost model calc (rough): expected token ops +1.8% for free if we keep smaller hedges; paid unchanged. We'll run a 1h extended to check.

lee: can we add a quick sampler to trace mixed-batch compositions? Want per-batch vector: [routes_in_batch], [max_seq, mean_seq], kernel_flavor. Helps repro.

alex: good idea — added a lightweight batch-tracer flag to canary (off by default). Will collect samples for 5%.

infra-bot: rollout update: canary traffic bumped to 5% for hedge-canary-3 at 09:48 UTC. Monitoring p95, kv-hit, kernel_switch_rate.

maria: after tracer enabled, found ~60% of problematic batches were mixed free+paid when inter-request arrivals overlapped. If we bias queueing to prefer homogenous route grouping (short hold window), mixed-batch fraction drops from 26% -> 6%.

alex: next steps:
- keep canary at 5% for 2h, watch p95 and kernel_switch_rate
- if stable, rollout hedging-lite to 20% (free zone only) and keep paid as-is
- open a follow-up to evaluate kernel stickiness impact on tail (A/B)

lee: also file a small perf test to simulate long-context bursts and validate kernel_cache eviction thresholds.

toni: ack — I'll schedule the perf test and validate no cross-pool kernel pollution.

alex: thanks all. Please add any weird traces to the thread. If we see regression, immediate rollback plan: revert hedging on free and set prefetch_delay_ms=0.

maria: noted. current plan looks promising — will post 2h metrics in this thread. :thumbsup:
